text: Our people are at the core of what we do, and the fighting spirit of our people determines how successful we are.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MINDEF and SAF does not take the commitment of our NSmen and NSFs lightly.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are invested in making the most of their time in NS and during their Operationally Ready National Service (ORNS) cycle.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We strive to bring out the best in every serviceman so that they can contribute more meaningfully and effectively with their abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is especially so, since today's SAF has a greater variety of roles to deal with an expanded spectrum of operations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of these new roles no longer depends solely on traditional notions of physical or operational fitness.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will require a mindset shift on how we think about the abilities of our servicemen.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Combat categorisation in the past tended to stream our servicemen based on what our people could not do.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But we can unlock our people's potential if we shift our focus to what they can do.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Coupled with continuous efforts to redesign roles and vocations, the Medical Classification System will enable our servicemen to be more meaningfully and effectively deployed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some may also be deployed to vocations that they were previously not eligible for.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The review of the Medical Classification System is being done in consultation with public medical specialists and members of our specialist advisory boards.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With greater precision, this ensures that our servicemen are deployed only to vocations that they are medically assessed to be suited for.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The robust safety and training system in MINDEF/SAF will continue to ensure that our servicemen in redesigned roles can train and operate safely.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We also want to better harness the talents of our NSmen with specific expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong asked about the talent pipeline into the DIS to tackle threats on our critical information infrastructure (CII).

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MINDEF recognises that many of our NSmen have honed their skills in the fast-changing cyber and tech domains through their private sector careers.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They have valuable experience we can tap on to augment the defence of Singapore's critical networks.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These teams are aligned to our CII sectors and will aim to strengthen the resilience of our CIIs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy will elaborate more on these NS cyber units in his speech.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Third is our commitment to the share of talent that MINDEF/SAF receives.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I am thankful that the public service continues to allocate top talents to MINDEF/SAF so that they can lead the SAF to be ready for today's and tomorrow's challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I am also grateful to parents for continuing to entrust their sons and daughters to the SAF, and to schools for grooming the next generation of leaders.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Altogether, these expressions of commitment send a powerful signal of strong, whole-of-nation support for Singapore's defence to potential adversaries.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The third "c" is contributions from our wider community that lend strength to the SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This strength can be seen through a model of concentric circles.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the centre of the SAF is the high-readiness core of active-duty personnel, who will respond first in any contingency.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Thus far, we have talked about how we will better support the first two rings.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The importance of the third ring cannot be understated – the extent of support they offer to our second ring directly affects the commitment of our full fighting force.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must remember that a strong SAF cannot fight alone if our society has already crumbled under pressure.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is also important that we continue to build the resilience of our population to external forces and disruptions.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MINDEF will therefore step up engagements with these broader segments of society, to cultivate an entire population that is committed and prepared to defend Singapore, as part of wider Total Defence efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In support of this objective, SAFRA will review its mission to extend its engagement beyond active NSmen.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will reimagine SAFRA as a platform for defence engagement to include our former NSmen and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Minister of State Desmond Choo will speak about this later.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Dr Neo Kok Beng asked if we should redefine NS to include voluntary services in all uniformed groups, and to allow new citizens to participate.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While NS is the bedrock of our defence and will remain so, we can do more to encourage a culture of participation in defence through volunteerism.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Everyone has a part to play, and everyone who lives in Singapore should have opportunities to volunteer in some way.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Volunteers play a key role in supporting the SAF and Singapore's defence by taking on meaningful roles that complement the work of Regular personnel.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, the defence volunteer base is more diverse and dynamic than ever.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of our volunteers, some of whom are also our Operationally Ready National Servicemen, have valuable real-world experiences and industry expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Having a strong volunteer core also adds to our deterrence.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Potential adversaries would think twice if they knew they would face a populace that is committed, skilled and prepared to defend Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy will speak more about this in greater detail on how we intend to expand the size and scope of the SAFVC.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The fourth "c" has to do with connections – our diversified portfolio of international partnerships, which have advanced Singapore's and SAF's interests in crucial ways.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our fundamental ability to build connections and partnerships rests on a capable and credible SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: No one will want to partner someone who is unable or unwilling to pull their own weight and make a contribution.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Thus far, our partnerships have provided valuable opportunities, such as opening up new training areas overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This has allowed us to overcome our space constraints for complex, large-scale exercises.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These partnerships also provide access to advanced defence technologies to equip our warfighters.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Shawn Huang asked about MINDEF's approach to building defence relations in a more volatile and complex landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: My response is that we cannot take our connections and value to others for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must strengthen our value proposition to others as their needs will also shift and for that, we must keep evolving our approaches with them for us to remain relevant.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First and fundamentally, we must develop a clear-eyed perspective of their challenges, their needs, for us to be able to come up with compelling value propositions to partner them.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As a small country, we cannot simply be "neutral".

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Staying neutral will induce greater pressure on us from others to take their side and narrow our strategic space.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We do not want to "choose sides" either, which makes us a proxy for others, takes away our agency and renders us irrelevant.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The only way is to develop an approach based on consistent principles that we believe in and are good for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must convince others that our view of the world serves their interests too, so that they will want to work with us.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In a more unpredictable environment, it is all the more important for our views to be principled and consistent.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They signal to others that we will be steady and reliable partners despite changing circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, we must capitalise on Singapore's unique value proposition.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For instance, it has become even more important now for countries to communicate and share their concerns candidly.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have been able to convene dialogue and encourage common understanding on issues, often away from the public glare.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Where we can be useful, Singapore is glad to play our part in providing a space for open and meaningful discussions amongst other partners.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But key to our value proposition here is that we must maintain our reputation as a trusted and reliable partner.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On Mr Gerald Giam's point, the new threats on the horizon also present new opportunities to find common ground with non-traditional partners and open up new areas for collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The threats that AI and cyber tools can pose are almost universal to every country.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But this also means that we can collaborate with new partners from anywhere in the world, so long as they share the same views as us and want to shape the norms responsibly.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are several other examples of shared interests, such as counter-information campaigns and the protection of critical underwater infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These are areas where we can work with other like-minded states to learn from their experiences, and for us to share ours, for our mutual benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Another area where we can work with new partners is in defence technology.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Indeed, the more uncertain geostrategic environment has also raised the risk of supply chain disruptions but it has also presented new opportunities for us to be able to work with partners that previously may not have considered us as their partner of choice.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Other countries recognise the same challenge and that is why in this environment, we will also see a more diverse global defence industry.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Advanced science and tech innovation is now pursued by a wider range of countries, as well as companies – not just traditional defence companies, but also start-up firms and tech giants, especially for dual-use technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These developments all present new opportunities for MINDEF to work with them.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For instance, we have expanded our defence tech partnerships with various countries.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These developments show how we have found opportunities to work with new partners to shore up and strengthen our resilience in areas that meet our needs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To do all these, we need to ensure that our people deeply understand the world as it is, and are able to pinpoint the concerns and aspirations of others.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Every day of peace is another day where the dangers of complacency heighten, as Mr Alex Yam mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must never let this happen under our watch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, as Defence Minister Mr Chan has outlined, we face an increasingly complex world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore has reaped the peace dividend as a result of constant vigilance, diplomacy and active risk management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our defence must continue to stand strong on lasting foundations and NS remains the cornerstone of Singapore's defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As our world changes, we will continue to enhance the SAF and we must keep strengthening NS to stay effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: From enlistment, through full-time service, through to as Operationally Ready Servicemen and even beyond their active years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want to optimise how people can contribute to Singapore's security throughout their entire NS journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about how we are going to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They complete their final-year internship while serving in the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This means that they can pursue their studies whilst putting their learning into practice in NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We now have five such schemes, including our newest partnership with Ngee Ann Polytechnic launched last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This latest tie-up trains students as Army Engineers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Other servicemen can also take up Work-Learn Schemes after they enlist.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These programmes, run with our institutes of higher learning, let servicemen serve full-time NS while earning diplomas or university credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our most recent tie-up was launched last year with the Singapore Maritime Academy, where it trains Naval Warfare System Specialists in marine systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As we create more opportunities for servicemen to gain skills during NS, these skills must be recognised beyond their service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked how this is being done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will start a trial with selected SAF Training Institutes from the second half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Industry-relevant skills will be mapped in each serviceman's passport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This provides Government-verified records of the skills they have attained in NS and this will help boost their employability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong asked whether NS allowances can be pegged to labour market standards such as the LQS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MINDEF regularly reviews allowances and incentives for our national servicemen, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As an example, the allowance for a Recruit in Basic Military Training increased 65% in the last 10 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But NS allowances are just one part of many initiatives to recognise national servicemen, which are not available to Regulars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, NS HOME – HOME stands for HOusing, Medical, Education – which is designed to support housing, healthcare and education needs of our National Servicemen through top-ups to their Central Provident Fund, Post-Secondary Education Accounts (PSEA) accounts and LifeSG credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NSmen and their families also enjoy annual tax relief.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, now, on the comparison to Local Qualifying Salary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must also understand what the LQS is and what the LQS is not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As the Ministry of Manpower has explained, the LQS determines the number of local employees counted towards a firm's Work Permit and S Pass quota entitlement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The LQS is an administrative tool that ensures local workers are employed and paid meaningfully in the employment context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is not a minimum wage or general salary benchmark for all forms of service in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We should not draw equivalence between salaries and NS allowances because there is a fundamental difference between the two.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A salary is a transaction for labour services rendered by a worker to compensate for work done, and meet living expenses and commitments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NS is a unique civic duty and contribution by all able-bodied Singaporean men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While we acknowledge that serving NS involves opportunity cost, we should not erode our social compact and the ethos of service by casting it as an employer-employee relationship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For NSFs, the state takes care of the vast majority of their basic needs such as accommodation, food and equipping.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The NS allowances, which we regularly review, are designed to support NSFs' personal upkeep and other incidentals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NSFs who require further financial assistance due to personal circumstances are supported through the financial assistance schemes in the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These are layered upon what they can also get outside through the Ministry of Social and Family Development's ComCare schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I encourage any NSFs facing difficulties to speak with their commanders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I can assure them that the SAF will do its utmost to assist.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We deeply value the contributions that our national servicemen play in defending Singapore, and we remain committed in ensuring that our allowances and support measures remain relevant and meaningful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When servicemen transition to their 10-year Operationally Ready NS journey, they are building expertise in their civilian careers in a variety of sectors and exposures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, they can serve in NS roles that draw on the skills that they have gained in their jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We do this through the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This covers more than 20 areas such as legal, cyber, strategic communications and more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Take ME4A(NS) Aslam Bin Mohamed Johan, for example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Aslam is a Software Engineer with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) who specialises in system design and the development of digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Aslam previously served as a driver in the 1st SAF Transport Battalion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He was redeployed to the SAF C4 and Digitalisation Command in 2024, where he now applies his technical expertise to strengthen the SAF's digital systems and enhance operational effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is what we mean by optimising our servicemen's contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Instead of a one-size-fits-all deployment, we are matching individuals' professional expertise with roles where their skills can best serve Singapore's defence needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Another area where we are harnessing niche skills is cyber defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many of our NSmen today are skilled cybersecurity professionals who bring valuable real-world experience and industry expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are all aware of how critical cyberwarfare is to a country's national security and we have seen how Singapore's critical infrastructure comes under threat from time to time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are not immune to these attacks and we need to draw on the best talents that Singapore can provide among our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am pleased to say that many have come forward to offer their skills to defend Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Their expertise matters and can make a real difference – not just to the SAF, but to Singapore's broader cyber defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These teams will strengthen our capabilities, bring new ideas and approaches, and complement existing forces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will deploy them to support the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore in defending Singapore's CII.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This covers vital sectors such as telecommunications, power and transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One such example is ME4(NS) Lye Han Wei.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He is a manager in Cyber Threat Intelligence and Response from the Infocomm Media Development Authority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He will be part of the Telecommunications Sectoral Cyber Defence Team, bringing expertise and experience in niche areas such as operational technology, cybersecurity governance and threat detection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NSmen like Han Wei will contribute meaningfully to our national efforts to strengthen our cyber defence, offering specialised knowledge that would be difficult to replicate through traditional military training alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This represents a more coordinated, proactive approach against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, we are enabling better skills-matched deployment of our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These pathways enable NSmen to contribute more meaningfully to national defence by applying the expertise that they have developed in their civilian careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Lee Hong Chuang and Miss Rachel Ong asked about how we are involving the community and wider society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The defence of our nation is a shared endeavour that goes beyond those who serve NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our deterrence and mission success, if ever called upon, relies on the understanding and support of the wider Singapore society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Whether at the National Day Parade or at the recent Singapore Airshow, you can see Singaporeans from all walks of life show their sense of pride, embodying the spirit of Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many Singaporeans and residents want to contribute to our defence in different ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They want to play a meaningful role in keeping Singapore safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, beyond NS, we will be expanding avenues for women, Permanent Residents, new citizens and foreigners to step forward and play their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Just as NS has served Singapore well to foster cohesion and a sense of national identity through their service to defence, we want to expand the opportunity and potential to do the same with this initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This brings all volunteers in MINDEF, SAF and our related organisations under one common identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SG Defence Volunteer Network will focus on two key areas initially.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, we will expand civilian volunteer pathways by creating new opportunities across MINDEF, SAFRA, Defence Collective Singapore and our other agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Volunteers can contribute in ways that better match their skills, interests and life stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, we already have volunteers contributing specialist skills in military law, defence science, strategic communications and even museum guiding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year, we started the National Education Ambassadors scheme that lets individuals with a passion for Total Defence speak to students, youths and the public, covering all six pillars of Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also started the Total Defence Champions initiative this year to engage communities on how to respond during crises and disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Second, we will enhance military volunteer pathways through the SAFVC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SAFVC lets Singaporean women as well as PRs deepen their understanding of national defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They contribute directly to Singapore's security, strengthening our collective sense of ownership and responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sanjeev Kumar asked for an update on the SAFVC and whether MINDEF and SAF intend to expand opportunities for volunteerism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SAFVC marked its 10th anniversary last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will integrate the SAFVC more closely into SAF units to fulfil operational tasks alongside SAF personnel beyond peacetime support functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am glad that Mr Sanjeev has also noted how our SAFVC were deployed side by side alongside our SAF troops in Exercise Wallaby last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This gives volunteers a better understanding of how the SAF operates and lets them contribute practically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They can find inspiration from the many SAFVC Volunteers (SVs) today who serve with deep commitment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One example is SV2 Delhaye Geoffrey Jean-Raphael Georges, an Auxiliary Security Trooper, and his wife, SV1 Felicia Ang, who serves as a Bridge Watchkeeper.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Both of them joined the SAFVC to do their part for Singapore and serve as positive role models for their three children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For Delhaye, volunteering was also a way for him to deepen his roots in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since 2023, Delhaye has been based in Dubai for work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He relocated there with Felicia and their three children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Despite being overseas, both continue to serve whenever they are back in Singapore and they have contributed significant service days over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Their commitment reflects strong dedication to Singapore, regardless of where life or work takes them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Another example is SV2 Diana Lau, a nurse with Alexandra Hospital's Urgent Care Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: She volunteers as a medical trainer in the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During a training session, she noticed a trainee showing signs of heat stress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: She drew on her nursing background to help the medical team provide timely care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Her swift actions helped to ensure training could continue safely and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Diana continues to serve passionately with the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: She volunteers significant time each year while balancing a demanding nursing career.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our volunteers play an important role in strengthening Singapore's defence and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But safeguarding Singapore ultimately requires a whole-of-society effort, especially during crises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond operational roles in the SAFVC and specialist roles in MINDEF, we are expanding community-level volunteer participation through Total Defence initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Hazlina and Miss Rachel Ong asked about these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One key example is Exercise SG Ready, our annual Total Defence exercise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It strengthens the preparedness of Singaporeans and communities to respond to crises and disruption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It focused on readiness for degraded digital connectivity and prolonged power outages – things that we often take for granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But in an actual hybrid conflict, communications and power, are exactly the first two things any aggressor would want to take out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, this exercise provided a timely platform for whole-of-Government agencies as well as some businesses to test their plans and pilot new capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It encouraged everyone – individuals, community groups, businesses and students – to plan for disruptions, prepare to respond and play a part to keep Singapore strong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As part of the launch, the Public Warning System "Important Message" signal was broadcast nationwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Vehicles island-wide received broadcast alerts on their Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) 2.0 On-Board Units – the first public testing of this capability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A pilot community mobilisation activity was conducted at two HDB blocks in Tampines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Total Defence Champions and People's Association Community Emergency Response Team Volunteers engaged residents and shared what to do during disruptions and prolonged outages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More than 250 schools simulated disruptions to get students to think about their roles in Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many businesses used the exercise scenario to conduct table-top exercises or simulate disruptions at their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These efforts, let their employees, and sometime, members of the public, better appreciate how such disruptions affect life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To Ms Hazlina's point about people not being born here but choose to be here, I assure her that many of these participations in Exercise SG Ready also include PRs and foreigners who work alongside Singaporeans, especially during our business tabletop exercises to develop Business Continuity Plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, this is one way in which we involve the wider community, whether they are Singaporeans, PRs or foreigners, living here, to be prepared for any disruption that may come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through these experiences, we strengthened our resilience against unexpected situations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These examples reflect the growing ways Singaporeans and residents can contribute to defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, when we introduced NS in 1967, we proved that a small nation's defence could rest on the commitment of all its people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, as cyber threats and hybrid warfare challenge us in new ways, we must call again on the whole-of-society and use all skills available to defend Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our Pioneers built our nation and our defence over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, the Minister of State will next speak on how we continue to support the NS community and strengthen community support for defence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Chairman, when we discuss national security in this Chamber, we often focus on the hardware.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: We talk about the next-generation platforms, digital threats, and shifting geopolitical tides.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: But the true foundation of our defence does not lie in our armouries, and as our security landscape transforms, the institutions that connect our NS community with the broader society must transform as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about plans for SAFRA to better engage our wider Singaporean public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Today, I will outline SAFRA's evolving role in strengthening Singapore's defence ecosystem, transforming from what was once seen primarily as a social club into a part of a vital, nation-wide defence movement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: The strength of NS as an institution has always rested on the contributions of our national servicemen and the unwavering support of their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It is the worker who puts down his tools, the teacher who leaves his classroom and the father in the heartlands who trades his weekends for a uniform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: That is why SAFRA was built in 1972, not just as a collection of buildings for social purposes, but as a testimony to our shared recognition and support, and a place to celebrate the enduring bonds forged through service to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: After operating out of a temporary space in Prince Edward Lane, SAFRA's first purpose-built clubhouse opened in Toa Payoh in 1975.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: This was during the formative years of Singapore, when social amenities remained modest and country club memberships were exclusive, expensive and out of reach for most Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: From the very beginning, SAFRA has made its membership accessible to every national serviceman, a recognition of our fundamental belief that service to nation deserves recognition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: When then-Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew opened the first clubhouse, he shared his vision for SAFRA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: He stated that more clubhouses would be established in key residential areas because "the well-being of the SAF reservist includes the well-being of his family".

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: That insight remains as relevant today as it was then.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: By the mid-1970s, membership quickly pushed to 10,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: SAFRA has adapted and innovated with each new clubhouse, ensuring that it stayed true to its mission by providing relevant, affordable and accessible offerings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Each clubhouse has developed amenities and programmes to suit the region it serves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: But buildings and membership numbers are not and should not be the true measure of SAFRA's success and performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: The true measure lies in whether our servicemen feel supported, whether their families feel appreciated, whether Singaporeans understand and believe that NS is not an abstract policy, but a shared responsibility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: The security landscape around us is changing rapidly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Threats are no longer confined to conventional battlefields.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: We face cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns, and attempts by foreign actors to exploit social divisions and erode trust in public institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: These threats are designed not only to weaken our capabilities, but to weaken our cohesion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: And in such an environment, the strength of our defence depends not only on the SAF's operational readiness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It depends on trust, between servicemen and society, between institutions and citizens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked how we can ensure defence remains a shared national commitment across generations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: This is where SAFRA's role becomes even more critical.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It must become an organisation that empowers NSmen to build trust and community-wide support for defence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: What sets SAFRA apart from the other social clubs is its deep association with NS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It draws upon bonds forged in uniform – bonds of shared hardship, shared responsibility and shared pride.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: But as our operating environment evolves, SAFRA too must evolve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It cannot remain only a provider of lifestyle and recreational facilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It must become a bridge, connecting our citizen soldiers with the broader community they protect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It must help every Singaporean understand that defence is not the responsibility of a few.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Mr Alex Yam also asked how MINDEF can work with organisations like SAFRA to ensure that defence remains a shared national commitment for the whole-of-society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Its programmes and engagement will serve NSmen for each stage of their lives as they progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: For pre-enlistees, the transition into NS can be daunting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It marks a significant milestone, one that demands maturity, resilience and sacrifice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: These fairs also serve NSmen who are seeking new employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: For NSmen with young families, we recognise the unique opportunity to connect generations through shared understanding of NS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Many of us in this Chamber know the reality of the work cadence today, missing the occasional full-day family outing, or coming home late from camp.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It is this quiet, steadfast support at home that keeps our servicemen and women going.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: These camps provide families with a meaningful glimpse into NS experience while introducing the concept of Total Defence to children from an early age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: These camps also create valuable opportunities for NSmen fathers to share their NS journey with the next generation, explaining not just what they do in NS, but why they serve, and who they serve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: What started out as pilots in 2023 have now become heavily demanded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Many participating families have expressed their appreciation, with some even becoming "repeat customers".

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: When these programmes are ready, SAFRA will also invite NSmen and other volunteers to support as facilitators, ambassadors and storytellers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: These NS Experience camps foster deeper understanding of an NSman’s contributions, and will strengthen the community's appreciation of the values of service and sacrifice that underpin our defence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Even when NSmen complete their ORNS training, their journey with SAFRA continues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: For these former NSmen or "NS alumni", as we call them, SAFRA is developing an initiative that goes beyond simply providing event spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It will partner with the SAF to create meaningful sessions where senior commanders share the latest developments in defence and strategic insights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: These cohesions will serve a dual purpose: maintaining the social bonds forged during service, while strengthening our broader defence network by keeping NS alumni informed and connected to the current defence issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: This ensures that the bonds and commitment forged during NS remain a vital part of our national defence fabric long after active duty ends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: We also know some of the most meaningful support from the NS community does not come from just programmes alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: NSmen bring with them diverse professional experience, such as finance, technology, healthcare and education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: This is defence in action – servicemen supporting servicemen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: SAFRA will expand such peer-to-peer platforms, encouraging more NSmen to step forward as mentors, facilitators and industry connectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: In doing so, we strengthen not only individual livelihoods, but also the bonds that underpin our defence community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: I have spoken about how SAFRA will strengthen its support for the NS community by curating engagements across life stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: SAFRA will continue to enhance the way we serve the NS community by delivering good, accessible and quality lifestyle offerings and recreational facilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: The upcoming SAFRA Bayshore is an example of this commitment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Next, let me turn to how SAFRA will deepen community engagement through NSmen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: First, SAFRA will go beyond lifestyle offerings to bridge defence and community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: While access to military camps must understandably remain controlled, we can bring defence closer to the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Mr Alex Yeo asked about MINDEF’s plans to leverage SAFRA's network to raise defence awareness in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: In the coming years, SAFRA clubhouses will house defence heritage galleries that will tell the stories of our Services and Formations through its walls and spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Our NSmen and their contributions will not be forgotten.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It will also engage club tenants as partners, inviting them to become defence advocates through partnership programmes and exclusive promotions that celebrate our defence heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Our goal is simple: everyone who visits a SAFRA clubhouse in future should leave feeling more connected with Singapore’s defence story.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: SAFRA will also work with community and defence partners to organise road shows for the public to learn more about the various aspects of defence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: This will include supporting the SAF in scaling up its SAF-School Partnership Programme (SSPP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: SSPP was started in the 2000s to deepen students’ understanding of the SAF through interactions at school visits or experiential learning by visiting camps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: The public can look forward to the inaugural SAFRA Community Defence and Resilience Festival in early 2027.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: This will be accompanied by showcases of military equipment from the SAF and include exhibits where the community can learn more about our defence capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: For the fitness enthusiasts – and there are many in this Chamber – you can look forward to an NS-inspired Fitness Festival in the later part of this year, complete with NS-themed obstacle courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: It will comprise a fitness race for 3,000 participants, as well as a series of programmes in the lead up to the race.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: These programmes will be co-organised with the People’s Association and NTUC, and we expect this to reach another 27,000 participants across the island.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: We will be mindful to invite Mr Alex Yeo, Mr Alex Yam and Mr Patrick Tay to join us in our version of Hyrox.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: We know that, ultimately, building community support for defence requires leadership from those who have served.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Today, NSmen volunteer across SAFRA’s steering committees and regional initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: They shape programmes, organise outreach and build partnerships with grassroots organisations, schools and local businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Through these expanded volunteer networks, we are building something more than a collection of programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: We are strengthening a culture, a culture where service is valued, where sacrifice is understood and where defence is embraced as a shared mission.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: We are strengthening the very foundation of our national defence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: Mr Chairman, this is how we strengthen the bonds between NSmen and their communities, building a more resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
text: I am confident that together, we can and will succeed in this vital defence movement that our nation’s security depends on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Minister highlighted that strong, conventional capabilities remain central to a credible deterrence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: We have also heard about how the SAF is adapting to emerging threats.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Can MINDEF also provide an update on how the SAF plans to stay capable and technologically advanced, particularly in terms of its higher end capabilities?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, if I may make a couple of points in response to Mr Yip Hon Weng's clarification.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, I do not intend to list out all the conventional capabilities and their timeline.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think we will do that in good time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As I mentioned, we will only reveal the capabilities at a time of our choosing, when it is operationally useful.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second point, I think we also would encourage everyone to move beyond the concept of what we call conventional and non-conventional capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As far as SAF is concerned, they are just capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There will be a spectrum of capabilities that will be required to meet our enduring, emergent and evolving challenges.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the past, the type of scenarios that MINDEF/SAF has to contend with is probably fair to say, a bit more limited.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, the range of scenarios that MINDEF/SAF has to contend with has expanded greatly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Within these expanded scenarios and each of the different scenarios, we will need a mix of different capabilities to respond.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are things that our potential adversaries will also take notice.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But what is beyond these conventional capabilities will be the other capabilities that I have alluded to, which we may not always reveal to others.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Previously I have mentioned that some of the ideas that we have worked on started some 10, 20 years ago.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And sometimes for some of these classified capabilities, it is the length of time required for us to develop breakthroughs in the science and technology for us to develop such capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, at a time where it is appropriate, we will reveal more of such capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But as far as the conventional platforms are concerned, we will use our budget wisely to upgrade those where we can and to acquire new ones when we need to.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not always acquire new weapons systems only.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I want to assure Members of the House, it is not just about acquiring new, shiny platforms.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Very often, we acquire platforms that meet our needs and we retrofit them according to our operational needs, just as we have done for the C130s, the Leopards and other platforms.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I had filed this as a Parliamentary Question later, but I thought I would raise it today.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy said we should not erode the social compact and the ethos of service by casting NS as an employer-employee relationship.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: But SAF Regulars serve the same mission and they are paid market rate salaries and CPF, so it does not erode their ethos of service.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I do not think duty and compensation are incompatible at all.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: The fact is that people who have no choice get paid less than people who do.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: The Senior Minister of State also framed accommodation, food, equipping as part of the compensation package.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I think these are just simply operational necessities for the SAF.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: The army feeds soldiers because hungry soldiers do need to fight.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Why can we not find it to pay our soldiers fairly?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, I understand Mr Tiong has filed a Parliamentary Question and we intend to answer the Parliamentary Question subsequently.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I would just like to say three things, since this is raised now instead of the Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It has existed for a long time and SAF will continue to build up our capabilities ahead of time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That has guided how I was brought up in the SAF and that will be how I continue to lead MINDEF/SAF.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Perhaps to share a story with the Members of the House.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have regularly visited our soldiers, including NSFs serving across the entire MINDEF/SAF establishment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Whenever I meet soldiers, 19, 20 years old, working in a classified unit, I will ask them this question, "What do you tell your parents about what you are doing?" I am proud to say I have consistently heard only one answer, and they do not have to rehearse this because I am the Minister for Defence.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They are matured enough to tell me that they will just tell their parents that they are serving their country, full stop.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sometimes, those who know the most say the least.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sometimes, those who do the most say the least.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I think those are wise responses from our NSFs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The SAF works on the basis that many of our systems, classified systems, are operated by NSFs and NSmen.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not disclose our capabilities and over the years it has been quite amazing that how generations of NSmen have been able to operationalise such capabilities without having to tell the world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I am proud of them, and I think this must continue to be the culture that we have in the SAF.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On NSF compensation, let me say that having served both NSF and as a Regular, I will be the first one to champion that we recognise the contributions of our NSFs and NSmen appropriately.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think those of us who have served in NS will be very careful to not use the word "compensate", because in truth, no amount of monetary compensation can be equated with the contributions of our NSmen.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not just the two years that they serve.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And many of our NSmen serve even beyond the two plus 10 years – they volunteer their services.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: What is the ultimate price for all this contribution?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not how much money we give them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Ultimately, it is the security and survival of Singapore that we are defending.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Yes, we will take care of our NSmen.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it is not just about NSF allowance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And when we have the budget space, we will do more, and I will be the first one to champion that we do more.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I do not want us to get into the wrong concept that this is a transactional relationship.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have never seen it so and I hope that generations of Singaporeans will continue to not see it so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not in our interest to cause invidious comparison or to bring this down, this sacred duty of serving our country into a transaction.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Of course, we will take care of our NSmen.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Of course, we will do more for the HOME awards.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Of course, we will do more for the NS credits, the tax incentive, wherever we can.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I appeal to Members of this House not to conflate duty with transaction.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Minister, I think some of the threats I had discussed, including terrorism and cybersecurity, are likely to be cross domain and involve other Ministries, such as the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), and potentially, MDDI.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Could the Minister share how MINDEF works with other Ministries to deal with these threats?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, indeed, as Mr Vikram Nair said, many of these threats are cross domain.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They do not just emanate from within the security domain.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And MINDEF will continue to work very closely with our MHA counterparts, MDDI.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have various standing arrangements from committees that look into the future to operational committees that look at actual operations, so that we can be ready, not just to handle the current ops, but also to anticipate the future ops.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue to do this, as to who takes the lead and who is the first among equals, it will depend on the operational context.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In certain instances, the civilian agencies will front it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The rest of the Government agencies, including MINDEF, will continue to support as a whole-of-Government, whole-of-nation effort.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In other more serious contingencies where MINDEF needs to front it, the other contingents will continue to support and we have standing operational structures on how we continue to operate this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, I must emphasise that it is not just about dealing with the contingencies, just as the recent cyber attacks have shown.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Likewise, when it comes to the issue of counter terrorism, it is not just about MINDEF or MHA capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Actually, what is the terrorist trying to do?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They are trying to psychologically shake us and take away the sense of normalcy that we have.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One of the most important thing that we need to do if we were ever under attack is to never allow the terrorists to achieve their aim of disrupting our way of life.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The psychological defence part is so important, which goes beyond MINDEF and SAF.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It requires a whole of society effort for us to make sure that we are inoculated.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have seen how the experiences of other countries have done.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, there is one particular country which has a standing policy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Whenever they are faced with a terrorist attack, and if the terrorist were successful in killing someone or bombing somewhere, they made it a point that within a few hours, they will make sure that the place is entirely cleaned up and people will go on with their life as per normal.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that, I think, is an aspirational standard that we should also strive towards.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: However, I seek his response regarding defence procurement audits by the AGO.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: A best solution mindset, which he mentioned, also requires external accountability and appropriate transparency.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: What specific initiatives exist to help startups pivot innovative solutions to bolster both national defence and commercial exports?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Actually, the AGO does audit MINDEF and the AGO has submitted reports to this House before of its audit of MINDEF processes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It will also require oversight from authorities beyond the direction of command.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is how we ensure that we get bang for the buck.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This process is robust, is rigorous, and the best testimony or a benchmark or an indicator is that you often hear that contractors complain about MINDEF/SAF.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is because we drive the hardest bargain.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, recently I was overseas for a meeting and I met up with one of the global defence majors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But you know why I still want your business?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because if I can get the MINDEF/SAF business, you are my reference customer." So, I quickly asked him, "so does that mean that I get a better price?" And indeed, MINDEF/SAF is often a reference customer and we want to maintain and upkeep our reputation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because they know that when MINDEF buys something, the process is robust.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we have those rules that I mentioned: operations come first, operations come last.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The start and end of everything has to do with our operational needs and no other considerations.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: No political interference, no political considerations, no other pecuniary things.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In order to negotiate such a deal to ensure our resilience, it is not just the upfront purchase.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Even if one day the supplier goes away, we must have the technical capability to continue to upgrade those platforms for the 20 years and beyond.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the Member's second point about working with research agencies beyond MINDEF, DSTA and DSO.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, we have done that systematically over the years.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have established relationships, established labs with our own universities and also some overseas universities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I would just say that we will have to be very careful with how we handle such relationships.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While increasingly, there are a lot of technologies that can be dual use, not every technology provider will be comfortable with such a posture.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When we approach partners to work with MINDEF, we must do it sensitively, respecting their comfort zone.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we should also be careful not to put our partners in positions that they find difficult.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Otherwise, nobody will want to work with us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, it is not just established companies, it is not just startups, it is also research labs in Singapore and beyond.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The Minister updated the House earlier about the importance of keeping pace with technological advancements as well as hybrid threats, especially in the cyber domain.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: While we have talked a lot about how we grow defence internally and get our people on board, could I ask the Minister if he could share with the House, what is the status of our international cooperation in terms of defence, growing our defence capability and also threat assessments?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, if I may build on the point that I have raised in my answer.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Yes, the threats have broadened and deepened, but I must say that the opportunities for us to work with new partners have also expanded.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Perhaps I illustrate this with my recent trip to the Munich Security Conference.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I am one of the few Asian representatives in a otherwise mainly European conference.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The question is what are we doing there?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But more importantly, what can we offer there?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And before I go for any conference, I always ask myself this question, "Why do people want to talk to us?" The fact that we want to talk to people is quite obvious, but why do people want to talk to us?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And after meeting them, will they still want to talk to us?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that goes to the core of the value proposition.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But we share the same challenges when it comes to cyber.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Another example, information warfare: where people use information to try and divide societies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, there are no shortage of examples and live operations in Europe, the Baltic Scandinavian countries.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And suddenly, they find that there are partners that can work with them are beyond their European region.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that was why last year, at the Shangri-La Dialogue, we saw the highest participation of the European countries in our Shangri-La Dialogue for many years.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because they now see opportunities to work with credible, trusted and reliable partners – and Singapore is one of them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And suddenly, we find that we have new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are just examples of how we are able to look for new opportunities to work with new partners.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But all these are contingent on this basic: we must clearly understand what people are thinking and why are they thinking what they are thinking, so that we can come up with a timely value proposition, so that I can answer the two questions that I always challenge myself before I go into a meeting: "Why does he want to talk to me?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And will he still want to talk to me after the meeting?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: I have a clarification for Minister of State Desmond Choo.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Given the importance of physical readiness for pre-enlistees, as well as NSmen, preparing for the Individual Physical Proficiency Test, and even the proposed Hyrox that you mentioned, whether SAFRA has considered extending its outreach by partnering with relevant agencies to provide or support exercise facilities and structured fitness programmes in neighbourhood parks, so as to make training more accessible and convenient for those who may not live near an existing SAFRA club?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: My Radin Mas constituency would be more than happy to partner with SAFRA to implement a trial in one of our neighbourhood parks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: He will also be invited for our version of Hyrox.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Indeed, the value of SAFRA is not only in these clubhouses; it is not only the physical amenities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: It runs very good amenities too, but the core of it is the people who run the programmes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: It is no longer enough or prudent for us to keep building clubhouses, so we must make sure that our programmes can travel.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: And we can imagine ourselves working with partners at People's Association, NTUC and like-minded partners to bring the programmes where our enlistees might be or whereby NSmen can work out together with their children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: So, what is the end result that we want?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: What we want is a whole-of-Singapore effort, partnering different associations, institutions, whether it is People's Association, NTUC, SAFRA coming together and, of course, not forgetting our HomeTeamNS partners, providing the best platform whereby NSmen can find it easy for them to get ready, whereby everyone, as they come in contact with us, feel a stronger sense of defence; and at the end, we are stronger for it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: So, for all our Members here, those of you have been quite excited by my Hyrox thing, you are also invited for NS experience camps.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: You can bring your children to come along too and indeed, we are looking for constituency partners to roll out these camps, making sure they are accessible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: NSmen can go into camp with their children, inculcating defence right from a very early age.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister of State Choo, I must say I am quite excited myself about the Hyrox.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: It is clear that the international environment we are used to operating in is at a turning point.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: As strategic competition between the US and China intensifies, other countries and middle powers are also repositioning themselves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: So, what is our strategy for navigating this increasingly complex geopolitical landscape?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: And as Singaporeans, how can individuals and the broader society stay prepared and play a part?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Every time I talk to my servicemen, I talk to my Public Service officers, I always ask them to come back and tell me three things, wherever they go, in that country: what has remained the same, what has changed and what do you think is going to change?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I see this as a discipline that all of us as Singaporeans can contribute to.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because in today's uncertainties, it is not just the role of MINDEF and MFA to sense-make what is happening around the world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All of us as fellow Singaporeans, all of us can make a contribution, no matter which corner of the world we go to.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Do not understand just what they do but understand why they do what they do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And always come back, tell us the three things: what has not changed, what has changed and what will change?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because we will constantly need to find new value propositions, be it major powers or China.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, constantly, regularly, when I meet my US counterparts and my Chinese counterparts, it is the same approach.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I try to understand what is going on in their thinking, where we can partner them to make a contribution for our mutual shared interests.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if there are differences that we need to manage, how can we manage them sensitively while we continue to manage to hold on to the big picture to work for each other's mutual benefit.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is the same for the US; it is the same for China.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And at every stage of their development, there will be evolving priorities that we need to keep, we need to be sensitive to and we need to keep finding those new value propositions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it is with that spirit that I think we can stay vigilant to the challenges and also be ready to seize the opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If there is one thing that we share between the MINDEF and SAF speeches today is that, yes, the world is in a state of flux.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are many challenges, but that does not mean that we have no agency.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That does not mean that there are no new opportunities for us to entrench our relevance to the world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So long as we go in with our eyes open, take a realistic approach to what the world is, constantly challenge ourselves to find and create those value propositions, we will be in good stead.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Last but not least, I must say this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They find us serious-minded, thinking long term and honest with integrity.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are valuable attributes that we must continue to hold in order for us to entrench our position as a credible partner with real capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Nobody will talk seriously to anyone without real capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When we say we want to partner another defence establishment to develop science and technology or do research in a particular area, we must inspire confidence in others that we will deliver.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is the basis upon which we will continue to build our relationships with the rest of the world, continue to entrench our relevance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And on that note, I thank Members of the House for your support for our defence, of NS.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And may we continue to work on this together to build Singapore for the next lap.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Yip, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Chairman, I thank the Minister, the Senior Minister of State, the Minister of State, and the men and women of MINDEF and SAF, especially our NSmen, for securing the peace and stability we often take for granted.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: At the same time, we must strengthen total defence because a capable SAF and a resilient society go hand in hand.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Chairman, with that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
